long_biography.plain_text:
Raised between Swiss precision and Italian aesthetics, Muller trained at the Geneva School of Watchmaking and built an early reputation restoring exceptional pieces for collectors and auction houses. He began presenting complicated wristwatches in the 1980s, bringing mechanisms associated with pocket watches onto the wrist and making the tourbillon visible from the dial side.

His partnership with case-maker Vartan Sirmakes turned that workshop practice into an international luxury brand. Their company paired technical inventions with the curved Cintrée Curvex case and the later Crazy Hours display. A strategic dispute followed an acquisition approach: Muller wanted to sell, Sirmakes refused, and Muller eventually disposed of his entire stake. The namesake brand continues under other management. Muller no longer owns it or participates in daily operations, leaving his earlier creative work and founder tenure as his defining commercial legacy.
